## Summary

Eisman sees AI investors becoming more demanding about cash flow, competitive moats and rising capex. He contrasts strong equipment demand with pressure on hyperscaler finances and software valuations, reviews several earnings reports, and explains why banks do not diversify his AI exposure. He also describes funding shorts.

Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.

## Framework and tools

- Evaluate earnings quality by removing investment gains.
- For long-cycle equipment suppliers, orders and backlog can matter more than quarterly EPS.
- Separate an operating beat from the market's expectations for guidance.
- Look through bank profits to their AI financing exposure.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Alphabet adjusted EPS, cloud growth and free cash flow
- GE Vernova orders and backlog
- Corporate quarterly EPS/guidance
- Short-sale cash-flow illustration
